newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Holds steady, crude supports.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Holds steady, crude supports.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was actively quoted on Monday, but traders said they did not expect major price movements in the near term.
On late Monday, the 180-cst grade was traded at $99 per tonne for lifting August 9-13, compared with the last trading level of $100 per tonne last week.
The 380-cst was bid/offered at $96 per tonne for different dates. There were no deals on 380-cst. The same grade was offered at $96.50 on Friday.
Traders said crude gains boosted prices slightly earlier in the day but a lack of additional buying support other than a local trading company limited the upward momentum.
The trading company, which has said it is buying to supply term contracts, has bought to date some 12 cargoes on a steady basis since late June.
"There is no additional buying, so it's hard for prices to move up significantly," said one trader.
The market was waiting for results of two fuel oil tenders from Taiwan and Sri Lanka, traders said.
Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) will close a tender on Tuesday to sell 18,000-20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil for lifting July 22-23.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) will also close a tender on Tuesday to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent sulphur 180-cst fuel oil for August 1-5 lifting.
Late on Monday, no transaction was reported on the SIMEX fuel oil futures. August contract was bid/offered at $98.00/$99.00.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
